detailZh: Netflix发布新版迈克尔·舒马赫1994年F1纪录片预告片
Netflix发布了纪录片《Schumacher '94 - The Birth of a Legend》（舒马赫94：传奇的诞生）的预告片，这部新纪录片讲述了迈克尔·舒马赫的首个F1总冠军头衔
迈克尔·舒马赫与他的车队一起庆祝夺冠
Netflix已发布其即将推出的F1纪录片《Schumacher '94 - The Birth of a Legend》（舒马赫94：传奇的诞生）的预告片，该片将于10月2日全球首播。
这部德语纪录片长片由 LEONINE Documentaries 制作，Christin Freitag 执导，聚焦于迈克尔·舒马赫的首个冠军头衔。
新发布的预告片预览了1994赛季的幕后细节，这位德国车手在那个赛季赢得了他的第一个F1冠军，其中包括一些与这位七届冠军最亲近的人的见解。
他的妻子科琳娜·舒马赫在纪录片中占有重要篇幅。片中还包括对前贝纳通车队领队弗拉维奥·布里亚托利、前F1首席执行官伯尼·埃克莱斯顿、舒马赫的前经纪人威利·韦伯、前F1车手大卫·库特哈德以及德国资深播音员 Kai Ebel 和 Heiko Waßer 的采访。
这部Netflix纪录片的简介写道：“1994年是F1历史上的一个转折点：25岁的迈克尔·舒马赫在巴西赢得赛季首场大奖赛，开启了一段前所未有的职业生涯。”
“1994年是F1历史上最戏剧化、最激动人心的赛季之一，这一年间发生了许多影响深远的事件，例如埃尔顿·塞纳（Ayrton Senna）的致命事故，以及关于操纵比赛和不公平驾驶行为的指控。与此同时，一股真正的‘舒米狂热’（Schumi Mania）也席卷而来。”
剧情简介继续写道：“迈克尔·舒马赫（Michael Schumacher）的妻子科琳娜·舒马赫（Corinna Schumacher）以及他身边的其他人回忆起了那时的他。他们记得他在赛道上是一个毫不妥协的斗士，而在赛场之外则是一个敏感、富有同理心的人。
“一直是他情感支柱的科琳娜·舒马赫，还讲述了一段非凡爱情故事的开端——这段爱情至今依然牢不可破。”
粉丝们对这部纪录片的期待已经开始升温。“F1史上的最伟大车手，”一位粉丝在YouTube上简单地评论道，而另一位粉丝则开始了上映倒计时，写道：“还剩4周！”
detailEn: Netflix releases trailer for new Michael Schumacher 1994 F1 documentary
Netflix has released the trailer for "Schumacher '94 - The Birth of a Legend", a new documentary exploring Michael Schumacher's first F1 championship title
Michael Schumacher celebrates championship victory with his team
Netflix has released the trailer for its upcoming Formula 1 documentary, Schumacher '94 - The Birth of a Legend, ahead of its global premiere on 2 October.
Produced by LEONINE Documentaries and directed by Christin Freitag, the German-language feature focuses on Michael Schumacher's maiden championship title.

The newly released trailer previews behind-the-scenes details from the 1994 season, in which the German driver claimed his first F1 title, and includes insights from some of those closest to the seven-time champion.

His wife, Corinna Schumacher, features heavily in the documentary. It also includes interviews with former Benetton team principal Flavio Briatore, former F1 chief executive Bernie Ecclestone, Schumacher's former manager Willi Weber, former F1 driver David Coulthard and veteran German broadcasters Kai Ebel and Heiko Waßer.

"1994 marks a turning point in Formula 1 history: 25-year-old Michael Schumacher wins the first grand prix of the racing season in Brazil, setting the stage for an unprecedented career," the synopsis of the feature film from Netflix reads.

"The year 1994, which is among the most dramatic and exciting racing seasons in Formula 1 history, featured impactful events such as Ayrton Senna's lethal accident, as well as accusations of manipulation and unfair driving manoeuvres. At the same time, a true 'Schumi Mania' emerged."

The synopsis continued: "Michael Schumacher's wife, Corinna Schumacher, and other people close to him reminisce about him at that time. They remember an uncompromising fighter on the race track and a sensitive, empathic man off the course.
"Corinna Schumacher, who has always been his emotional support, also offers insight into the beginnings of an extraordinary love story - one that is still going strong today."
Excitement for the documentary is already building among fans. "The GOAT of F1," one fan commented simply on YouTube, while another began the countdown to the release, writing: "4 weeks left!"

detailZh: 皮埃尔·加斯利失去摩纳哥大奖赛领奖台席位，国际汽联上诉法院裁定
国际上诉法院裁定，皮埃尔·加斯利在摩纳哥大奖赛收到的、此前曾被撤销的处罚依然有效
国际汽联国际上诉法院（ICA）裁定，阿尔派车队一级方程式车手皮埃尔·加斯利最终失去了他在摩纳哥大奖赛的领奖台完赛成绩，他因在维修通道超速而受到的处罚维持不变
加斯利是在该赛事中因维修通道超速被处罚的多名车手之一，但后来发现维修通道的测量数据不准确，前两个计时点之间存在77厘米的误差——这也是处罚数量异常之多的原因
当奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里和乔治·拉塞尔等人因为在比赛中执行处罚而蒙受损失时——拉塞尔的处罚执行方式有误，这位梅赛德斯车手因此被处以穿过维修区的处罚——加斯利的两个五秒处罚则被加到了他的比赛成绩上，使他从第三名跌至第七名。这一时机意味着阿尔派车队得以申请复审。
FIA赛事干事随后于6月12日推翻了这些处罚，加斯利因此恢复了第三名的位置。但对于那些在比赛期间执行处罚的车手来说，这并非可行的选择。
红牛车队的伊萨克·哈贾尔和迈凯伦车队的皮亚斯特里蒙受了损失，分别从第三和第四名跌至第四和第五名。因此两支车队都向国际上诉法院（ICA）提起了上诉；这一举措得到了小红牛车队（其两名车手均在成绩榜上各失去一个位置）和英国赛车运动协会（Motorsport UK）的支持。
法院于周五裁定处罚有效，因此加斯利重新跌回第七名，而他的同胞哈贾尔则继承了第三名——这位红牛车手在赛后已经庆祝过这个位置。
加斯利（阿尔派车队）、哈贾尔（红牛 比赛车队）
ICA的部分推理依据是，阿尔派无法完全确定地证明Gasly在维修区内实际行驶的距离比（不准确地）测量出的距离更远，因此其在两个计时点之间较短的时间可能反映出“更短的路线、更高的速度，或两者的结合”。
然而，ICA确认，其他车手已经服完处罚“不能成为取消一项不合法处罚的障碍，因为那些处罚是由车队自行斟酌和选择而执行的。若以会造成体育不公平为由持相反观点，反而会与体育公平相悖。”
阿尔派对这一决定表示“失望和沮丧”，仍然坚称Gasly没有任何过错，不应受到任何处罚。
车队在声明中表示：“车队对国际汽联国际上诉法庭就2026年摩纳哥大奖赛结果所作出的裁决表示失望和沮丧。”
“尽管我们不同意这一决定，并且仍然完全坚持10号车在比赛期间任何时候都没有超过维修区限速，但车队接受近期在巴黎举行的听证会上裁判小组作出的决定。”
“虽然这一结果并非我们所期望的，因为我们认为自己受到了不公正的处罚，但车队将坚定地专注于继续提升赛道上的表现，并仍处于一场激烈而胶着的冠军争夺战中。”
“这一结果不会削弱车队在赛季结束前实现其目标的努力和动力。”
与此同时，国际汽联（FIA）在一份声明中坚称，其赛事干事做出错误决定并不一定负有责任，但该联合会承诺将审查其相关流程。
声明中写道：“国际汽联注意到国际上诉法院（ICA）今天就8月25日星期二听证会（案件编号 ICA-2026-06-07-08-09）做出的决定。”
“国际上诉法院的裁定支持了迈凯伦F1车队（迈凯伦 F1 Team）和红牛车队（红牛 比赛）针对摩纳哥大奖赛第99号文件中赛事干事决定所提出的上诉，实际上推翻了这些决定。”
“国际汽联正在审查当前一级方程式计时系统的方法和运作以及相关的规则事务。还将审查其他司法程序和运作，包括复审权以及上诉流程。”
“国际汽联（FIA）完全支持干事（Stewarding）工作流程，以及由多元化干事小组所具备的独立性和客观性，他们是全球赛车运动不可或缺的一部分。
“干事的裁决是在与法庭不同的环境下作出的，而法庭可以获得大量额外的法律顾问意见、辩论和证据。
“国际汽联干事不断审视其工作流程，并参与大量的专业发展培训。国际汽联干事会仔细研究国际上诉法院（ICA）的每一项裁决，以确保流程的持续改进。”
detailEn: Pierre Gasly loses Monaco GP podium, FIA’s Court of Appeal rules
The International Court of Appeal has ruled that Pierre Gasly’s Monaco GP penalties, which had been rescinded, do stand
Alpine Formula 1 driver Pierre Gasly has lost his Monaco Grand Prix podium finish after all, as his penalties for pitlane speeding stand, the FIA’s International Court of Appeal (ICA) has ruled.

Gasly was one of several drivers who were pinged for pitlane speeding during the race in the principality, but it emerged the pitlane measurements were inaccurate, with a discrepancy of 77cm between the first two timing loops – hence the unusual number of penalties.

While the likes of Oscar Piastri and George Russell lost out by serving their penalties during the race – incorrectly served in Russell’s case, with the Mercedes driver consequently incurring a drive-through sanction – Gasly’s couple of five-second penalties were added to his race time, dropping him from third to seventh. The timing meant Alpine was able to request a right of review.
FIA stewards subsequently overturned the penalties on 12 June, meaning Gasly was reinstated in third position. But this wasn’t an option for the drivers who served their penalties during the race.

Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar and McLaren’s Piastri lost out, dropping from third and fourth to fourth and fifth. Both teams therefore appealed the decision before the ICA; the move was supported by Racing Bulls, whose drivers both lost a spot in the classification, and Motorsport UK.
The Court ruled on Friday that the penalties do stand, so Gasly is back down to seventh, with fellow countryman Hadjar inheriting the third place the Red Bull racer celebrated post-race.
Pierre Gasly, Alpine, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

Part of the ICA’s reasoning was that Alpine couldn’t prove with full certainty that Gasly had travelled a longer distance in the pitlane than (inaccurately) measured, so its shorter time between the timing loops could reflect “a shorter path, greater speed, or a combination of both”.

However, the ICA confirmed that other drivers having served their penalties “cannot be an obstacle to the cancellation of an illegitimate sanction, because those penalties were served at the discretion and choice of the team. Admitting the contrary on the grounds that it would create sporting unfairness would in return be inconsistent with sporting fairness.”
Alpine has expressed “disappointment and frustration” with the decision, still adamant that Gasly did nothing wrong and was undeserving of any penalties.
“The team expresses its disappointment and frustration with the outcome reached by the FIA International Court of Appeal relating to the result of the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix,” a team statement read.

“While we disagree with the decision, and still fully maintain that Car #10 did not exceed the Pit Lane speed limit at any point during the race, the team acknowledges the decision of the judging panel from the recent hearing in Paris.

“While the result is not what we had hoped for, as we feel that we have been unjustly punished, the team is firmly focused on continuing to improve its performance on track and remains in a close and very competitive Championship fight.
“This outcome will not deter the team’s efforts and motivation in achieving its objectives by the end of the season.”
Meanwhile, an FIA statement insisted that its stewards weren’t necessarily to blame for making a wrong decision, though the federation pledged to review its processes.
“The FIA notes the decision today from the International Court of Appeal (ICA) in relation to the hearing of Tuesday, August 25 (case ICA-2026-06-07-08-09),” the statement read.

“The ICA decision upholds the appeals of McLaren F1 Team and Red Bull Racing against the decisions of the stewards contained in document 99 of the Monaco Grand Prix, effectively overturning those decisions.

“The FIA is reviewing the methodology and operation of the current Formula 1 timing system and the related regulatory matters. It will also be reviewing other judicial procedures and operations including the right of review and the appeal processes.
“The FIA is fully supportive of the Stewarding process and the independence and objectivity of the diverse panels of Stewards who are an integral part of global motorsport.
“Stewards’ decisions are taken in a different environment to that of the Court, whereas the Court has access to extensive and additional legal counsel input, arguments and evidence.

“The FIA Stewards constantly review their processes and take part in extensive professional development. Every decision of the ICA is carefully examined by FIA Stewards ensuring a process of continuous improvement.”

detailZh: 阿尔派车队F1车手加斯利的两项五秒处罚被重新恢复，因此他再次失去了2026年摩纳哥大奖赛的领奖台名次。
这一决定是在迈凯伦和红牛就FIA撤销Gasly在摩纳哥因维修区超速而受到的两项处罚的裁决提出上诉之后作出的。
撤销Gasly处罚的决定是在阿尔派申请复审之后作出的。结果显示，Formula One Management在用于计算速度的维修区距离测量上出现了错误。
红牛和迈凯伦对这一改判提出上诉，认为事后更改测量基准损害了体育公平，因为各车队都是根据原始测量数据来校准其维修区限速器的。
红牛车队的伊斯克·哈贾尔（哈贾尔）——本周末因手腕受伤缺席蒙扎站——因此递补获得2026年摩纳哥大奖赛的最后一个领奖台席位。
迈凯伦车队的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里（皮亚斯特里）在摩纳哥原成绩为第四名，当加斯利被恢复至第三名后，他被降到了第五名。
关键的是，皮亚斯特里是多名因在维修区超速而受罚的车手之一——但他不可能让处罚被撤销，因为他已经在比赛中执行了处罚。
不过，这位澳大利亚车手在摩纳哥站排名中将回升一位至第四名，排在小红牛车队的两位车手之前——而加斯利则被降至第七名。
阿尔派 F1车队发布的一份声明开头写道：“车队对国际汽联国际上诉法庭就2026年摩纳哥大奖赛结果所作出的裁决表示失望和沮丧。”
“尽管我们不认同这一决定，并且仍然完全坚持10号车在比赛期间的任何时候都没有超出维修区限速，但车队接受近日在巴黎举行的听证会上评审团的裁决。”
“虽然这一结果并非我们所期望的，因为我们认为自己受到了不公正的处罚，但车队将坚定地专注于继续提升赛道上的表现，并继续投身于一场激烈而势均力敌的锦标赛争夺之中。”
“这一结果不会动摇车队在赛季结束前实现其目标的努力和动力。”
detailEn: Alpine Formula 1 driver Pierre Gasly has had his two five-second penalties reimposed and therefore lost his 2026 Monaco Grand Prix podium finish, again.
The decision comes after appeals were brought by McLaren and Red Bull against the FIA’s decision to rescind Gasly’s pair of penalties for pitlane speeding in Monaco.

That decision to rescind Gasly’s penalties was made after Alpine petitioned for a right of review. It emerged that Formula One Management had made a measurement error relating to the pitlane distance used to calculate speed.

Red Bull and McLaren appealed the reversal, arguing that changing the measurement benchmark retrospectively undermined sporting fairness as competitors had calibrated their pitlane speed limiters using the original measurements.
Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar - out this weekend in Monza with a wrist injury - therefore receives the final podium place from the 2026 Monaco GP.
McLaren’s Oscar Piastri was classified fourth in Monaco and demoted to fifth when Gasly was reinstated to third.
Piastri, crucially, was one of several drivers who picked up pitlane speeding penalties - but could not have had his punishment rescinded as he served the penalties during the race.
The Australian will however move back up one place in the Monaco standings to fourth, ahead of the Racing Bulls pair - with Gasly now demoted to seventh.

“The team expresses its disappointment and frustration with the outcome reached by the FIA International Court of Appeal relating to the result of the 2026 Monaco Grand Prix,” began a statement released by the Alpine F1 team.

“While we disagree with the decision, and still fully maintain that Car #10 did not exceed the Pit Lane speed limit at any point during the race, the team acknowledges the decision of the judging panel from the recent hearing in Paris.

“While the result is not what we had hoped for, as we feel that we have been unjustly punished, the team is firmly focused on continuing to improve its performance on track and remains in a close and very competitive Championship fight.
“This outcome will not deter the team’s efforts and motivation in achieving its objectives by the end of the season.”

总工程师折原慎太郎解释说，这次升级完全集中在内燃机上，不过在赞德沃特，他带着一张纸来参加媒体会，以此强调他绝对不想谈论在马力或圈速方面的收益。
在蒙扎，折原已经不再随身携带那张纸了，这让他开玩笑说：“现在你们可以问我所有问题了！”
“在马力方面，本田仍然不愿意透露任何数字，尽管当Motorsport.com问及此事时，折原确实表示，这第一次ADUO升级的进展完全符合预期。
“所以我们曾在荷兰引入了一款新规格的引擎，我们观察到了性能上的一个进步，正如我们各项指标所预期的那样，”他说，“我们已经确认了在测试台架上看到的结果，所以这是我们在荷兰发现的一个积极因素。
不过，在赞德沃特的比赛周末也表明，仍然有工作需要完成。
“另一方面，我们在驾驶感受方面发现了一些可以改进的地方。因此我们更新了燃烧特性，然后准备了数据设置和工具来适应这些新的燃烧特性，以获得更好的驾驶感受。”折原继续说道。
“但这还不足以让车手们满意。所以这绝对是我们在荷兰站发现的改进点。”
本田的折原慎太郎在接受Motorsport.com罗纳德·沃尔丁的采访时说道。
驾驶感受指的是车手从动力单元获得的感觉。这种感觉尚未完全达到本田的预期，也未能在一整圈中保持完全一致，这并不令人意外。
折原已经在斯帕-弗朗科尔尚赛道接受Motorsport.赛车运动网独家采访时提前透露了这一点，这意味着本田知道，在将第一套ADUO升级件带上赛道之后，仍然有工作要做。其中一些工作已经在赞德沃特赛后的十天里完成了。
“我们把所有数据带回了测试台架，我们也把所有车手的反馈带回了测试台架，”折原继续说道。“他们在HRC樱和研发中心进行了一些测试，以改进我们的控制系统，从而获得更好的可驾驶性。所以本周末的主要重点将是在蒙扎赛道确认这些应对措施。”
当被问及可驾驶性问题具体是什么时，这位本田一级方程式项目的总工程师解释说，这是一个涉及多个不同方面的复杂问题。
“如果说到可驾驶性，它包含换挡、制动阶段的燃烧稳定性，还有发动机反拖（引擎制动）阶段的燃烧稳定性以及扭矩响应，”折原详细说明道。“很多因素共同构成了可驾驶性，我们需要改善整个领域。”
“所以主要问题在于我们如何控制燃烧，以及如何获得稳定的燃烧。这是提升我们整体可驾驶性的主要着力点。”
虽然本田主要是在寻求新燃烧特性下的稳定性，但阿斯顿·马丁的赛道事务负责人迈克·克拉ック强调，可驾驶性也与底盘有关。
“可驾驶性不仅是动力单元的问题，也是底盘的问题，所以我们需要在这方面协同工作，努力弄清所有事情，”克拉克说。
“你想要追求最优，但同时也希望在不同程度的能量回收、不同程度的制动以及不同程度的降挡下都能保持一致。这可不是一件容易的事。”
“我认为这是每支车队都在学习的东西，而且每支车队确实都必须针对赛道的每一段进行优化。归根结底，在谈到可驾驶性时，我们不能只看动力单元，还要看整体。底盘和动力单元的所有部件都牵涉其中。”
随着这些方面的改善，本田认为还能从赞德沃特的升级中再榨取一点性能，不过这不会是一个大的进步，因为不会再有新的硬件改动。
“尽管如此，我们认为通过优化数据，我们还有提升性能的空间。”折原说。“我们为这条赛道带来了一些标定方面的改动，以最大化我们的性能，但这不会是一个大的变化，只是优化而已。”
detailEn: The key area Honda still needs to improve with its new F1 engine
Progress with Honda’s first ADUO upgrade of the year is fully in line with expectations, although the Japanese manufacturer says there is still one area it needs to work on: driveability
After Adrian Newey’s first major upgrade package in Hungary for Aston Martin, Honda introduced its first power unit update of the Formula 1 season in Zandvoort.

Chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained that the upgrade was entirely focused on the internal combustion engine, although in Zandvoort he brought a piece of paper with him to his media session to stress that he absolutely did not want to talk about the gains in terms of horsepower or lap time.
In Monza, Orihara no longer has that piece of paper with him, which prompted him to joke: “Now you can ask me everything!”

Honda still does not want to disclose any numbers when it comes to horsepower, although Orihara did say the progress with this first ADUO upgrade is fully in line with expectations, when asked about it by Motorsport.com.

“So we introduced a new spec engine in the Netherlands and we have observed a step forward in terms of performance, as expected in our metrics,” he said. “We have confirmed what we saw on the dyno, so that was a positive thing that we found in the Netherlands.”
However, the race weekend in Zandvoort also showed that there still was work to be done.

“On the other hand, we found some things to improve in terms of driveability. So we have updated our combustion characteristics and then we prepared the data settings and the tools to adapt to these new combustion characteristics to get better drievability,” Orihara continued.
“But it was not enough to satisfy the drivers. So that is definitely our improvement point that we found in the Netherlands.”
Shintaro Orihara, Honda, during an interview with Ronald Vording, Motorsport.com

Driveability refers to the feeling drivers get from the power unit. The fact that this feeling is not yet entirely where Honda wants it to be, nor fully consistent throughout the lap, does not come as a surprise.

Orihara had already flagged this at Spa-Francorchamps in an exclusive interview with Motorsport.com, meaning Honda knew it still had work to do after bringing its first ADUO upgrade to the track. Some of that work has already been carried out in the 10 days since Zandvoort.

“We brought back all data to the dyno and we brought back all driver feedback to the dyno,” Orihara continued. “They have carried out some testing in HRC Sakura to improve our controls to get better driveability. So the main focus point for this weekend will be to confirm those countermeasures in Monza.”
Asked exactly what the driveability issues are, Honda’s chief engineer for the F1 project explained that it was a complex picture involving several different aspects.

“If you say driveability, that contains the shifting and the combustion stability during the braking phase, and also during the engine braking phase and torque pickup,” Orihara detailed. “A lot of things combine into driveability and we need to improve the full area.
“So the main issue is how we control our combustion and how we get stable combustion. That is the main focus point to improve our full driveability.”
While Honda is primarily looking for stability with the new combustion characteristics, Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack stressed that driveability was also linked to the chassis.
“Driveability is not only a PU topic, driveability is also a chassis topic, so we need to work together on this, trying to understand everything,” Krack said.

“You want to go for the optimum, but also you want to be consistent with different levels of regen, with different levels of braking, and with different levels of downshifting. It's not an easy exercise.

“I think it's something that every team is learning and that every team really has to optimize for each section of the track. At the end of the day, when speaking about driveability, we must not only look at the PU but also at the whole thing. All the elements of the chassis and the PU are involved.”

As these aspects improve, Honda believes it can also extract a little more performance from the Zandvoort upgrade, although this will not amount to a major step as there will be no further hardware changes.

“Still, we think we have some room to improve performance by optimizing the data,” Orihara said. “We have brought some calibration changes for this track to maximize our performance, but it's not going to be a big change, just optimizing.”

items.originalTitle: 多梅尼卡利谈缩短比赛、冲刺赛及F1未来
items.summaryEn: At Monza, F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said F1 will not stand still, with the future focused on technical development, the calendar, manufacturer relations, sprint races and attracting younger audiences. He stressed that the risk for F1 is becoming complacent.
detailZh: 斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利谈缩短比赛、冲刺赛与F1的未来
F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利就规则、制造商、冲刺赛以及年轻观众等问题阐明了未来的指导方针
一级方程式赛车不想停下来回味这一格外积极的历史阶段的数字。这就是斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利在蒙扎想要重申的信息，内容涵盖从锦标赛的技术未来到赛历的演变，还涉及与制造商的关系、冲刺赛以及触达越来越年轻的观众群体的必要性。
“风险在于变得自我封闭，”F1的首席执行官解释道。“我们不能满足于今天取得的成功。我们必须继续理解为什么我们能变得如此强大，并保持脚踏实地，要知道我们仍有许多方面可以继续成长。”
核心议题之一涉及未来的规则。F1和国际汽联（FIA）即将开始研究下一代动力单元和单座赛车的特性，而当下的产业环境与现行规则制定时相比已发生了深刻变化。
多梅尼卡利强调：“在讨论我们今天正在经历的规则变革时，似乎未来是由电气化来定义的。但如今情况已不再如此。我们要做的就是理解如何正确地应对和解读这一变化。”
关键在于在大厂商的需求与F1不应完全依赖其产业战略之间找到平衡。“一方面我们必须保证厂商的参与，但另一方面，如果他们的优先级有所不同，我们必须懂得如何做到独立。如果厂商们今天决定离开，我们将面临一个大问题。”
因此，未来有可能转向技术复杂度更低的方案。“一个复杂度更低的项目，显然要在成本和性能目标的前提下，有助于实现独立。”多梅尼卡利还指出了他认为至关重要的两点：“我坚信要把可持续燃料置于技术项目的核心，并朝着更轻的赛车方向前进，因为我们希望看到车手能够真正把一辆必须掌控在他们手中的机器推向极限。”
多梅尼卡利对缩短F1比赛持开放态度

对体育产品本身的更广泛反思也在讨论之中。近几个月浮出水面的想法之一是略微缩短大奖赛的比赛距离，对于这一可能性，多梅尼卡利并没有关上大门。“我的立场非常简单，而且是从一个技术层面的考虑出发的。如果我们说的是，看起来也就是，减少几圈的话，那么在我看来，这也符合年轻人对长篇内容越来越缺乏耐心的趋势。我认为，如果我们说的是减少两三圈，不会有负面影响。如果变成更大幅度的削减，那就是另一回事了，但在这个范围内我不反对。”
这与冲刺赛推出时的理念相同，冲刺赛最初连多梅尼卡利本人也有些疑虑。“作为F1的‘老古董’，当这个方案被提出时，我是第一个持怀疑态度的人。但数据并没有推翻它：推广方、媒体和车迷中的绝大多数都已经接受了这一赛制，并认为它充满活力。”
因此，冲刺赛将继续成为F1的一部分，尽管多梅尼卡利排除了类似MotoGP那样每个周末都设置冲刺赛的情景。“冲刺赛的数量将少于赛事总数的一半，”他明确表示。“年轻人越来越欣赏一种周五就有实质比赛内容的周末形式。老牌车迷——我自己也属于其中——可能对练习赛也感兴趣，但对普通观众来说，周五就有排位赛意味着有更多的内容可看。”
“我必须说实话，这些数字让我感到惊讶，因为它们在强劲增长，”多梅尼卡利说。“基米不仅带来了赛道上的竞争力，还带来了一大批此前从未关注过一级方程式的人。他是一个年轻人，却以一种年轻人特有的轻松姿态面对巨大的责任。他身上有着与他同龄的孩子能够产生共鸣的自然与清新。”
将高峰关注转化为持久成功
然而，多梅尼卡利坚称，有必要将这些关注高峰转化为持久的关系。“我们必须避免这只是一次增长峰值，随后便离我们而去。最大的挑战在于弄清楚如何让那些第一次前来的观众保持联系。有些社群并不了解我们，我们有义务去建立一级方程式文化。”
这一愿景还包括锦标赛在地域上的扩张。多梅尼卡利提到中国、南美、远东和非洲是具有巨大增长空间的地区。“非洲正在给出重要的信号，我们希望很快能就此传达一些重要的消息。”
1993年南非大奖赛上，Hill领先于Zanardi。
最后，还有一个更紧迫的赛历问题，卡塔尔和阿布扎比仍然得到确认，但正处于观察之中。“赛历目前就是你们所知道的那样。我们正在密切关注局势，因为如果不能完全保证安全和可操作性，我们将不得不做出其他决定。各车队完全了解最新情况，与他们的对话是持续不断的。”
因此，即使处于扩张阶段，Domenicali仍将快速反应的能力视为应对未来风险的主要解决方案：“事情变化如此之快，如果你没有能力做出反应，你就会在一瞬间失去大量时间。我们绝不能冒的风险就是停止寻找有能力的人、新鲜的想法和新的视角。当你一直在同一个池塘里钓鱼时，钓到的鱼总是一样的。”
detailEn: Stefano Domenicali on shortening races, sprints and F1’s future
F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali sets out the guidelines for the future on regulations, manufacturers, sprint races and a young audience

Formula 1 does not want to stop and contemplate the numbers of a particularly positive historical phase. This is the message Stefano Domenicali wanted to reiterate at Monza, ranging from the technical future of the championship to the evolution of the calendar, via the relationship with manufacturers, sprint races and the need to reach an increasingly young audience.

“The risk is becoming self-referential,” F1’s CEO explained. “We must not be satisfied with the success we have today. We must continue to understand why we have become so big and keep our feet on the ground, knowing that there are still many dimensions in which we can grow.”

One of the central themes concerns the regulatory future. F1 and the FIA will soon begin to consider the characteristics of the next generation of power units and single-seaters, in an industrial context that has changed profoundly compared to when the current rules were defined.

“When the regulatory change we are experiencing today was addressed, it seemed that the future was defined by electrification. Today that is no longer the case,” Domenicali stressed. “It is up to us to understand how to react and interpret this change in the right way.”

The point is to find a balance between the needs of the major manufacturers and the need for F1 not to depend completely on their industrial strategies. “On the one hand we must guarantee the presence of the manufacturers, but on the other, if they were to have different priorities, we must understand how to manage to be independent. If the manufacturers decided to leave today, we would have a big problem.”

Hence the possibility of moving in the future towards less complex technical solutions. “A less complex project, obviously while respecting cost and performance targets, helps to be independent.” Domenicali also indicated two points he considers fundamental: “I strongly believe in keeping sustainable fuels at the heart of the technological project and in moving towards a lighter car, because we want to see drivers who can really push to the limit a machine that must be in their hands.”
Domenicali is opening to shortening F1 races

Also on the table is a broader reflection on the sporting product. Among the ideas that have emerged in recent months is that of slightly reducing the distance of grands prix, a possibility on which Domenicali has not closed the door. “My position is very simple and starts from a technical consideration. If we are talking, as it seems, about a few laps, for me it also goes in the direction of the fact that young people tend to be less and less present for long things. I don’t think there would be a negative effect if we are talking about reducing by two or three laps. If it became something more significant it would be a different discussion, but in this perspective I am not opposed.”

It is the same philosophy that accompanied the introduction of sprint races, initially met with some perplexity even by Domenicali himself. “I am the first who, as a Formula 1 dinosaur, had doubts when we proposed this. But the data did not contradict it: promoters, media and fans, in the vast majority, have digested the format and consider it dynamic.”

Sprint races will therefore continue to be part of F1, although Domenicali ruled out a scenario similar to MotoGP, with one every weekend. “They will be [at] fewer than half” of the events, he specified. “Young people increasingly appreciate a weekend in which there is already something that counts on Friday. Long-standing fans, and I include myself among them, may also be interested in a practice session, but for the general public having qualifying already on Friday means having more content.”

“I have to tell the truth, the numbers are surprising me because they are growing strongly,” Domenicali said. “Kimi has brought not only competitiveness on track, but also a wave of people who did not follow Formula 1 before. He is a young man who faces an enormous responsibility with a lightness typical of young people. He has a naturalness and freshness in which kids his age can recognise themselves.”
Turning peak interest into lasting success

Domenicali, however, insisted on the need to turn these peaks of attention into a lasting relationship. “We must avoid it being a growth spike that then leaves us. The great challenge is to understand how to keep connected those who show up for the first time. There are communities that do not know us and we have an obligation to build a Formula 1 culture.”

This scenario also includes the geographical expansion of the championship. Domenicali cited China, South America, Far East and Africa as areas with significant room for growth. “Africa is giving important signals on which we want soon to communicate something significant.”
Hill leads Zanardi during the 1993 South African GP

Finally, there remains the issue of the more immediate calendar, with Qatar and Abu Dhabi still confirmed but under observation. “The calendar, at the moment, is the one you know. We are monitoring the situation because, if safety and operability are not guaranteed in full, we will have to take other decisions. The teams are absolutely up to date, the dialogue with them is continuous.”

Even in a phase of expansion, therefore, Domenicali identifies the ability to react quickly as the main solution to future risks: “Things change so quickly that, if you are not able to react, you lose a lot of time in an instant. The risk we must not run is that of stopping looking for competent people, fresh ideas and new points of view. When you keep fishing in the same pond, the fish is always the same.”

items.originalTitle: F1 5MJ规则将导致蒙扎最高时速低于匈牙利
items.summaryEn: The FIA has reduced recoverable energy to 5MJ under F1's new power unit rules to keep cars flat-out at Monza as much as possible, but the Italian circuit's top speeds in 2026 will still be lower than in Hungary.
detailZh: F1的5兆焦规则将如何导致蒙扎的极速低于匈牙利
国际汽联将可回收能量减少到5兆焦，以便让赛车在蒙扎尽可能多地全速行驶，但赛道上的景象仍会大不相同
蒙扎在一级方程式中可能以“速度圣殿”著称，但2026年意大利大奖赛上它将呈现出不同的面貌
很早就可以明确，在使用新动力单元的情况下，蒙扎将是本赛季在能量管理方面最具挑战性的周末之一，因为这里直道很长，而用于回收能量的制动区很少
到目前为止，最低回收上限是为奥地利站设定的，每圈6兆焦耳，而在蒙扎将是5兆焦耳。这是合理的，因为仅靠刹车不足以回收这么多能量，否则直道上会出现大量“超级切油”（super clipping）——即电机发电机组在全油门时回收能量，导致赛车损失速度。国际汽联希望避免这种情况；同时松油滑行（lift-and-coast）也会减少。
另一方面，能量较少意味着赛车会在直道初期就把电池耗尽，然后逐渐切断电动机的辅助，直道剩余部分只靠内燃机工作——因此尾速要么趋于稳定，要么开始下降。
迈凯伦车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉和奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里解释说，在模拟器上，蒙扎的极速比匈牙利站更低，而在匈牙利站能量管理并不是限制因素。在布达佩斯，混合动力系统可以使用更长时间，速度可超过350公里/小时。
限制能量将使“超级切油”现象比银石、铃鹿和墨尔本站少一些，但不会完全消失——不过基米·安东内利认为“情况会比我们所有人预想的好得多”。其他一些车手则担心他们可能仍然需要在直道末端延迟降挡，以保持转速。
这将开启尾流（滑流）博弈，即使有主动空气动力学，它也可能非常有效——维斯塔潘和哈贾尔在斯帕-弗朗科尔尚赛道已经证明了这一点。阿斯顿·马丁赛道运营总监迈克·克拉克预测：“这里的反超与再反超的较量可能会创下历史之最，或者就像世界摩托车锦标赛一样。”
考虑到可回收的能量会比平时更少，即使在比赛中也是如此，超车模式将提供显著的动力提升，并使超车比过去的尾流减少阻力系统更容易——这就是为什么梅赛德斯在这里为安东内利接受了引擎处罚。
然而，风险在于使用超车模式后能量耗尽，因此可能会再次出现那种‘悠悠球’式的动态。
有一个因素不容忽视：一些车队已经达到了他们预期的赛季末下压力水平，因此制动距离缩短了，直道上的阻力增加了，过弯时的能量回收也减少了。这增加了对超级剃刀式切风（super clipping）和抬油滑行（lift-and-coast）的需求。这就是为什么在蒙扎减少可回收能量如此关键。
detailEn: How F1’s 5MJ rule will lead to lower top speeds at Monza than in Hungary
The FIA has reduced recoverable energy to 5MJ in order to keep cars flat-out as much as possible in Monza, but track action will still look very different
Monza may be known as the ‘Temple of Speed’ in Formula 1, but is set to look different at the 2026 Italian Grand Prix.

It was always clear that Monza was going to be one of the most challenging weekends of the season in terms of energy management with the new power units, with long straights and few braking zones to recover energy.

Up to now, the lowest harvesting limit had been set for Austria, with 6MJ per lap, but in Monza it will be 5MJ. This makes sense, as braking alone wouldn’t have sufficed to recover so much energy, so there would have been much super clipping on straights – when the MGU-K harvests energy at full throttle, so the car loses speed. The FIA wanted to avoid that scenario; there will also be less lift-and-coast.

On the other hand, having little energy means cars will drain the battery early on straights before gradually cutting off the electric motor’s assistance, leaving only the internal combustion engine active for the remainder of the straight – so speeds will either stabilize or begin to drop.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella and Oscar Piastri have explained that, on the simulator, top speeds were lower in Monza than in Hungary, where energy management wasn’t a limitation. In Budapest, the hybrid could be used for longer, with speeds upwards of 350km/h.

Limiting energy will lead to less super clipping than at Silverstone, Suzuka and Melbourne, though it won’t completely disappear – but Kimi Antonelli reckons “it’s going to be much better than we all anticipated”. Some other drivers fear they might still have to downshift late on straights to keep revs high.

This will open up the slipstreaming game which, even with active aero, could prove highly effective – was shown by Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar at Spa-Francorchamps. “The passing and repassing games probably will be a record of all times here, or like MotoGP,” Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack predicted.

Considering that the amount of recoverable energy will be lower than usual, even with in the race, Overtake Mode will provide a significant power boost and make overtaking easier than DRS used to – hence Mercedes taking an engine penalty with Antonelli here.
The risk, however, is finding yourself low on energy after using Overtake Mode, so that ‘yo-yo’ dynamic could be seen again.

One factor can’t be overlooked: some teams have already reached the downforce levels they expected for the end of the season, so braking distances are shortened, drag on straights in increased, and harvesting in corners is reduced. This increases the need for super clipping and lift-and-coast. That’s why reducing recoverable energy was so crucial in Monza.

keyPointsEn: Monza's long straights and few braking zones make it one of the most challenging weekends of the season for energy management with the new power units.

items.summaryEn: Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli has revealed a striking new helmet design for his home Italian Grand Prix, paying homage to MotoGP legend Valentino Rossi. The design is inspired by the iconic helmet Rossi wore to victory at Mugello in 2002.
detailZh: 安东内利 展示为意大利大奖赛准备的瓦伦蒂诺·罗西风格头盔
安东内利 公布了为他的主场意大利大奖赛准备的特殊头盔设计
一级方程式锦标赛领跑者 安东内利 公布了一款引人注目的全新头盔设计，用于他在意大利大奖赛的主场比赛，以此向 MotoGP 传奇人物瓦伦蒂诺·罗西致敬。
这位20岁的车手将在蒙扎赛道佩戴一款融入意大利国旗元素的设计，其灵感来自罗西2002年在穆杰罗夺冠时所佩戴的标志性头盔。该设计由 Drudi Performance 的 Aldo Drudi 创作，罗西绝大多数著名的比赛头盔都出自他之手。
安东内利在社交媒体上展示了这一设计，并确认该项目得到了罗西的认可。
“在家里比赛，我们使用特别的涂装，”这位梅赛德斯车手写道。“能够戴着受瓦莱启发设计的头盔比赛，是我一个特别的心愿。”
“当他们把2002年穆杰罗的头盔提供给我时，我立刻知道就是它了。Drudi Performance做了一项出色的工作，将它重新改造成今年家乡站比赛的这个版本。”
“感谢瓦伦蒂诺·罗西给我这个特别的机会。这是一种荣誉。我希望你们喜欢它，也希望我们能在赛道上看到它！明天见。”
Antonelli带着车手积分榜上59分的领先优势迎来自己的主场比赛周末，但他同时还有一次发车罚退，这给了对手们缩小积分差距的机会。
“这感觉非常特别，”Antonelli在周四的新闻发布会上谈到自己的主场比赛时说，“和去年相比确实大不一样。尽管要从队尾发车，我还是非常期待这个周末。
“但这也是摆在面前的一个大好机会，我非常期待。我觉得这个周末会非常令人享受。我将能够比我以前更加享受它。而且，希望我们仍然能跑出一场出色的比赛。”
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli unveils Valentino Rossi-inspired helmet for Italian GP
Kimi Antonelli has revealed a special helmet design for his home Italian Grand Prix
Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli has revealed a striking new helmet design for his home race at the Italian Grand Prix, paying homage to MotoGP legend Valentino Rossi.

The 20-year-old will take to the Monza circuit wearing a design incorporating the Italian flag and inspired by the iconic helmet Rossi wore to victory at Mugello in 2002. The design was created by Aldo Drudi of Drudi Performance, who was behind the vast majority of Rossi's famous race helmets.
Revealing the design on social media, Antonelli confirmed the project had Rossi's blessing.
"At home we race with special colours," the Mercedes driver wrote. "It was a special wish of mine to be able to race with a helmet inspired by Vale's.
"When they offered me the 2002 Mugello helmet, I immediately knew it was the right one. Drudi Performance did a fantastic job readapting it in this version for this year's home race.
"Thanks to Valentino Rossi for this special opportunity. It's an honour. I hope you like it and that we can see it on the track! See you tomorrow."
Antonelli heads into his home race weekend with a 59-point lead in the drivers' standings, but he also has a grid penalty, giving his rivals a chance to close the gap in the championship.

"It feels very special," Antonelli said of his home race during Thursday's press conference. "Definitely a lot different compared to last year. And I'm very much looking forward to this weekend despite starting from the back.

"But it's also a big opportunity ahead, and very much looking forward to it. I think it's going to be very enjoyable. I will be able to enjoy it much more than what I did previously. And, yeah, hopefully we can still do a great race."

items.titleZh: F1车手预计蒙扎意大利大奖赛体验将“怪异”且“令人困惑”
items.summaryZh: F1车手们预计本周末在蒙扎举行的意大利大奖赛将是一次“怪异”、“令人困惑”且“不太美妙”的驾驶体验。2026年能量受限的新赛车将在蒙扎遭遇迄今最极端的挑战。
items.originalTitle: F1车手预计意大利大奖赛将“怪异”且“令人困惑”
items.summaryEn: Formula 1 drivers expect this weekend's Italian Grand Prix at Monza to be a "weird", "confusing" and "not fantastic" driving experience. The energy-limited 2026 cars will face their most extreme challenge yet at the circuit.
detailZh: 一级方程式车手们表示，他们已经为本周末的意大利大奖赛做好了心理准备，在蒙扎赛道驾驶将是一种“怪异”、“令人困惑”而且“不太美妙”的体验。
能量匮乏的2026年一级方程式赛车将面临迄今为止最极端的挑战，而且这会带来一些奇特现象，其程度可能超出在其他赛道上所见到的情况。
从外部来看，一些不同寻常的因素可能并不那么明显，但车手们已经就他们的预期给我们提供了一些见解。
当2026年的一级方程式规则首次在模拟器上进行测试时，蒙扎被证明是赛历中最麻烦的赛道之一。
根据初步分析，人们普遍担心赛车在出弯时速度很快，但随着电池电量耗尽，速度会大幅下降。下降幅度之大，以至于车手们甚至在直道中途就不得不降挡。
对能量管理所做的调整——降低充电上限并限制电能释放——意味着现在直道上的速度曲线已经不同了。
这意味着赛车不会像我们过去看到的那样，从通常的350-360公里/小时的峰值速度下降30-40公里/小时。
相反，赛车的速度会趋于平缓，永远达不到过去那样的高速。
正如小红牛（小红牛）的阿尔维德·林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad）所说：“电量就是不够。我们在直道上其实并不慢，只是完全不使用（电能）而已。”
迈凯伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里表示，这种能量匮乏带来的一个奇怪后果是，蒙扎赛道的极速很可能反而比像亨格罗林这样的赛道更低。
“我觉得在我们的模拟器测试中，我们其实在匈牙利的前直道上比在这里还快，”他说，“这说不太通，但更多是因为我们根本没有能量可以消耗。”
模拟器测试显示，车手在主直道中段进入第一个减速弯时可能无需降挡，但在上坡进入阿斯卡里弯的入口处可能需要挂入七挡。
蒙扎周末之前的一个担忧是，由于这条赛道对能量如此匮乏，可能会迫切需要在各处大量使用超级切削（super clipping）技术。
这将意味着进一步降低像莱姆莫弯（Lesmo）和阿斯卡里减速弯（Ascari）这样壮观弯角的挑战性。
但国际汽联（FIA）为这个周末设定的5兆焦（5MJ）能量回收上限意味着超级切削不会太多地被使用，因为回收能量的机会实在非常有限。
正如皮亚斯特里所说："如果回收上限更高，我们就会在各处都使用超级切削，可能在每条直道末端损失30或40公里/小时的速度，但在[5兆焦]回收上限下，超级切削的量是正常或合理的。"
在2026年，F1车手们已经迅速学会了他各种聪明的办法，用现在这些赛车在能量匮乏的赛道上跑出速度。
在某些弯角放慢速度以便回收更多能量，如果这能在随后的直道上带来更多能量，反而可能带来好处。
这种现象在斯帕-弗朗科尔尚赛道达到了极端，因为一些车手发现，在像普雄（Pouhon）这样以前可以超高速通过的弯角提前松油门其实是最好的跑法，或者在某些弯角出弯时不以最大功率加速反而更有利。
一些车手认为蒙扎赛道的布局不提供这种聪明跑法的机会，因为回收能量的机会要少得多。
正如兰多·诺里斯所说：“我认为与斯帕的区别在于，那里有两条大直道，但中间有许多弯角，可以给电池充电，然后全部释放出来。
“不幸的是，这里有两条连续的长直道，而且即使在这两条直道之间也几乎没有任何弯角。所以根本没有能量，也没有动力。你没有充电的机会，所以就是慢。”
在蒙扎跑出一圈好成绩的关键，将是尽可能让电池保持最高的电量状态。
这不仅对排位赛中那些有效的计时圈很重要，对计时开始前的准备工作也同样重要。
由于一级方程式为出圈设定了9兆焦的充电上限，再加上车手需要让轮胎达到合适的工作温度，应该有充分的理由去推进节奏，而不是跑得超级慢。
然而，冷却圈被限制在标准的5兆焦。所以，如果车手在排位赛中采用推进-冷却-推进的策略，那么他们很可能需要跑得超级慢，以避免过早过度充电而触及上限。
“我觉得出圈会很慢，但不会慢得离谱，”他说。
“我认为让人不舒服的会是冷却圈，因为出圈和冷却圈的规则不同。所以，在冷却圈里你会跑得非常慢，以便给电池充电。”
车队和车手需要攻克的关键问题之一，就是如何最好地管理单圈开始阶段的电池电量。
如果在帕拉博利卡弯出弯时为了提升尾速而消耗过多电量，可能意味着你已经烧掉了太多能量，那么在驶向最后一个弯道时就会电量不足。
今年早些时候，车手们不得不琢磨在哪里最佳地提前加速，以便让他们的计时刻进入尽可能理想的状态。
这并不理想，因为这意味着每个人的做法都存在一定程度的不确定性。
作为五月份迈阿密站比赛期间推出的调整方案的一部分，这一功能被自动化了，允许车队通过编程来执行，也就是所谓的“自动K”（auto-K），由车队自行决定电池何时介入。
帕拉波利卡弯的出弯处就是会触发这种情况的区域，这意味着车手可以全油门出弯——但电池只会在预先设定的区域释放能量。
林德布拉德是认为这可能给排位赛带来一些风险的车手之一，因为做飞驰圈的赛车和即将开始飞驰圈的赛车之间可能存在很大的速度差。
“我们在赞德沃特稍微见识过一点，但靠着倾斜弯道，问题不大，”他说。
“当时的速度差有50到60公里每小时，所以你可以让开道路，让其他车手过去。
“现在的速度差甚至更大，这可能会变得有点危险。所以，开始飞驰圈并不容易，要做到满电输出、让轮胎进入状态。
“但即便只是从交通状况和安全性来看，这也不太好。我们需要更好的电池。”
detailEn: Formula 1 drivers have talked about being braced for a “weird”, “confusing” and “not fantastic” experience in driving Monza for this weekend’s Italian Grand Prix.
The energy-starved 2026 F1 cars are going to face their most extreme challenge so far, and it is going to throw up some quirks that may be a step beyond what has been witnessed at other venues.
From the outside, some of the unusual elements may not be so obvious, but drivers have already offered us some insight about what they expect.
When Formula 1’s 2026 regulations were first tried out on simulators, Monza proved to be one of the most troublesome tracks on the calendar.

Based on initial analysis, fears were widespread of cars blasting out of the corners and then speeds falling away as the battery power ran out. The drop-off was such that drivers were even having to change down gears halfway down the straights.
The tweaks that have been made to energy management – in reducing recharge limits and capping deployment – have meant the speed profile down the straights are different now.
It means that the car will not actually be suffering a 30-40km/h speed drop-off from the typical 350-360km/h peaks we have seen in the past.
Instead, they will flatline to never get near the old highs.
As Racing Bulls’ Arvid Lindblad said: “There's just not much battery. We don't actually go slower on the straights. We just don't use any.”
McLaren’s Oscar Piastri said that one of the bizarre consequences of the energy starvation was that top speeds would likely be lower at Monza than at a track like the Hungaroring.

“I think in our sim running we were actually quicker on the front straight in Hungary than we were here,” he said. “It doesn't make a whole lot of sense, but it's more that we just don't have the energy to spend.”
Sim running suggests drivers may not need to change down gears halfway down the main straight into the first chicane, but they may need to slip into seventh on the uphill entry to Ascari.
One of the fears ahead of the Monza weekend was that, because it was so energy starved, there could be a desperate need to super clip everywhere.
This would have meant further reducing the challenge of spectacular corners like the Lesmos and the Ascari chicane.
But the 5MJ harvesting limit that the FIA put in place for this weekend means that super clipping is not going to be called upon much, as opportunities to recover energy are so limited.

As Piastri said: “If the harvest limit was higher, we would be super clipping everywhere, probably losing 30 or 40 km/h at the end of each straight, but with the [5MJ] harvest limit, the super clipping is a normalish amount, or a reasonable amount.”
F1 drivers have learned quickly in 2026 the various clever ways to be quick at energy starved tracks with these current cars.
Being slower through some corners to help harvest more energy can deliver benefits if it delivers more energy on subsequent straights.

This is something that reached extremes at Spa-Francorchamps, as some found that lifting off in previously super-fast corners like Pouhon was actually the best way to go, or not accelerating with maximum power coming out of some corners was beneficial.
Some drivers think that the layout of Monza does not offer the opportunity for such a smart approach, as the chances to recover energy are much less.
As Lando Norris said: “I think the difference to Spa was that you had two big straights but you had lots of corners in-between that you could charge up and then deploy everything.

“Unfortunately here you have two long straights back-to-back, but even between them there's not really any corners. So, there's just no energy, there's just no power. You don't have an ability to charge, so it's just slow.”
The key to a good lap around Monza is going to be about maximising the state of charge of the battery.
This matters not only for laps that count in qualifying but also for preparations before the timing gets underway.

With F1 setting a recharge limit of 9MJ for out-laps, plus a need for drivers to get their tyres up to the right operating temperature, there should be every reason to push on rather than go super slow.

However, cool-down laps are capped at the standard 5MJ. So, if a driver is on a strategy of push-cool-push in qualifying, then the likelihood is they may need to go super slow to risk not over-charging early on and hitting the ceiling.
“I think the out-laps will be slow, but I don't think they'll be stupid,” he said.

“I think what won't be enjoyable is going to be cooldown laps, because the rules are different between out-laps and cool laps. So, in cool laps you'll be going very slow to try to charge the battery.”
One of the key aspects that teams and drivers are going to need to get on top of is how best to manage the battery for the start of the lap.
Deploy too much for a top speed boost out of Parabolica and it could mean you have burned too much energy, so you are left short on the run to the final corner.
Earlier in the year, drivers had to work out where best to accelerate before the timing line to start their laps in the best place possible.
This was not ideal as it meant there was a certain level of unpredictability about what everyone was up to.

As part of the package of in-season tweaks pushed through for Miami in May, this was automated to allow teams to execute this through programming of what’s become known as ‘auto-K’ where teams decide when the battery kicks in.
The exit of Parabolica is an area where this will take place, so means drivers will exit flat on the throttle – but the battery will only deploy in an area that is predetermined.
Lindblad is one who thinks this could pose some risks in qualifying if there is a major speed offset between cars on quick laps and those who are about to start.
“We saw it a bit in Zandvoort, but it was okay because of the banking,” he said.
“There was a 50-60 km/h speed delta, so you could get out of the way and let the guys through.
“Here it's even more - and it could become a bit dangerous. So, starting the lap won't be easy, to have it full, have the tyres ready.
“But even just from traffic, from safety, it's not great. We need a better battery.”
keyPointsZh: 从外界看，一些不同寻常的因素可能并不明显，但车手们已经分享了他们的预期。
当2026年规则首次在模拟器上测试时，蒙扎就是赛历上最棘手的赛道之一。
keyPointsEn: Some of the unusual elements may not be obvious from the outside, but drivers have already offered insight into what they expect.
When the 2026 regulations were first tried out on simulators, Monza proved to be one of the most troublesome tracks on the calendar.

items.titleZh: F1车队同意2027赛季将比赛距离从305公里缩短至290公里
items.summaryZh: F1车队已达成一致，计划从2027赛季起将比赛距离全面从305公里缩短至290公里，以应对新规则下燃油需求上升带来的问题。
items.originalTitle: F1车队同意2027赛季缩短比赛距离
items.summaryEn: Formula 1 teams have agreed a plan to cut race distances from 305km to 290km across the board from 2027, in response to problems caused by increased fuel demand under upcoming rule changes.
detailZh: 一级方程式比赛将在2027年缩短，各车队已同意一项将比赛距离全面从305公里削减至290公里的计划。
在为防止赛车出现能量匮乏而修改规则之后，明年的燃油流量率将会提高。
但这一旨在提升观赏性的举措给车队带来了其他麻烦，因为流经发动机的燃油越多，完成一场比赛距离所需的燃油就越多。
对于那些按照2026年要求设计了当前油箱尺寸、且不想在下赛季打造全新赛车的车队来说，这是一个问题。
成本上限中已作出相应安排，给那些计划沿用底盘的车队提供一些额外的开支自由度以便进行改装，但与此同时还采取了一些措施，尽量减少赛车预期的行驶里程。
在油耗流量调整方案获得同意后，各方开始讨论是否有可能将部分比赛的赛程缩短几圈，另外还作出了一项调整，即限制车手在进入发车格之前只能进行一次编队圈。
但在与车队就哪些比赛需要调整进行讨论的过程中，各方清楚地意识到，如果整个赛季的比赛距离各不相同，可能会产生一些意想不到的后果。
据了解，当时存在部分比赛演变成燃油经济性测试的风险。
因此，在国际汽联（FIA）与各车队进行对话之后，各方一致同意，整个赛季的大奖赛最好采用统一的比赛距离，就像现在这样。
据Autoracer.it最先报道，这一想法如今已获得各车队的一致支持，目前正在推进将其写入规则手册。
多年来，F1的比赛距离一直是完成超过305公里所需的最少圈数。唯一的例外（除了安全车起步的大奖赛之外）是摩纳哥大奖赛，其比赛距离为260公里。
各车队同意的这项明年生效的改动，将使所有比赛（摩纳哥除外）缩短至约290公里——也就是把各站比赛减少大约三圈。
虽然这一距离的调整得到了各车队的支持，但在写入2027年运动规则之前，仍需经过一个正式的程序。
这意味着需要向F1委员会提交修订后的规则，该委员会由车队、国际汽联（FIA）和FOM组成。一旦在该委员会获得批准，随后还需要国际汽联世界汽车运动理事会予以批准。
据了解，由于动力单元规则在如此晚的阶段进行修改所带来的妥协，比赛距离的缩短目前仅就下个赛季达成了一致。
不过，如果发现计划在2028年实施的额外燃油流量修改引发更多麻烦，各车队可能会决定将该距离维持更长时间。
detailEn: Formula 1 races are set to be shorter in 2027, with teams having agreed a plan to cut race distances across the board from 305km to 290km.
In the wake of changes being made to the regulations to stop cars being so energy-starved, fuel flow rates are being increased for next year.
But the move to improve the spectacle has triggered other headaches for teams, because more fuel going through the engine means more is needed to complete a race distance.
That was a problem for teams that had built their current fuel tank sizes around the 2026 requirements and did not want to make an all-new car for next season.

Allowance has been made in the cost cap to give teams that were planning to carry over their chassis some extra spending freedom to make modifications, but alongside this were also moves to minimise the distance cars were expected to run.

Once the fuel-flow tweak had been agreed, discussions opened about potentially reducing some race distances by a couple of laps, with a further change being made in limiting drivers to just a single formation lap before the grid.

But amid the talks with teams about which races needed to be targeted for adjustment, it became clear that there could be some unintended consequences if there was a variety of race distances throughout the season.
It is understood that there was a risk of some events turning into fuel-economy runs.
So, following dialogue between the FIA and teams, it was agreed that it would be better to have a universal distance for a grand prix throughout the season, as there is now.
As first reported by Autoracer.it, this idea has now received unanimous support from teams so moves are in play to have it added to the rulebook.

For years now, F1 race distances have been the fewest number of laps required to exceed 305km. The only exception to this (beyond when grands prix start behind the safety car) is the Monaco GP, which runs to 260km.
The change agreed by teams for next year would result in all races (apart from Monaco) being reduced to around 290km - so will pull the events back by around three laps.
While the change in distance has been supported by teams, it still needs to go through a formal process before it is put into the 2027 sporting regulations.

This means revised regulations need to be proposed to the F1 Commission, which is made up of teams, the FIA and FOM. Once approved there, it will then need ratification by the FIA's World Motor Sport Council.
It is understood that the reduction in race distance is currently only agreed for next season because of the compromise caused by the change of power unit rules at such a late stage.
However, teams may decide to keep it at that level for longer if it is found that the additional fuel-flow changes planned for 2028 cause further trouble.
keyPointsZh: 为防止赛车能量不足，新规则将提高明年的燃油流量，导致完成整场正赛所需燃油增多。
一些车队已按2026年规则要求设计了当前的油箱尺寸，不愿为下赛季打造全新赛车，缩短比赛距离可缓解这一难题。
keyPointsEn: To stop cars being so energy-starved, fuel flow rates are being increased for next year, meaning more fuel is needed to complete a race distance.
Some teams had built their current fuel tank sizes around the 2026 requirements and did not want to build an all-new car, so the shorter race distance eases that problem.

items.titleZh: F1意大利大奖赛首日：引擎话题主导围场
items.summaryZh: F1意大利大奖赛首日，蒙扎作为最依赖引擎的赛道，引擎相关话题成为围场焦点，The 比赛团队整理了首日的主要发现。
items.originalTitle: F1意大利大奖赛首日：引擎话题主导围场
items.summaryEn: On the opening day of the F1 Italian Grand Prix, engine-related topics dominated paddock conversations at Monza, the most engine-dependent circuit on the calendar, as The Race team gathered key takeaways from Thursday's activities.
detailZh: 没有哪条赛道比意大利大奖赛的举办地蒙扎更能与F1引擎性能画上等号。
因此，难怪在周四的车队围场里，关于尾流（及其相关战术）、引擎升级、甚至2026年F1赛车比赛性能的话题占据了讨论的主导地位？
以下是周五赛道行动开始前的最大要点：
无论排位赛结果如何，安东内利都将因动力单元处罚从蒙扎发车格的最后一位起步。
这意味着他在排位赛的发车位置方面没有任何实际可争取的东西，而在一个尾流被认为会带来优势的周末，如果车队要求，他愿意帮助队友兼总冠军竞争对手拉塞尔。（没有引擎处罚的勒克莱尔也会为法拉利队友汉密尔顿这样做。）
"这件事已经和车队讨论过了，是的，我们就一些事情达成了共识," 当The 比赛问到他是否愿意为Russell提供尾流牵引时，Antonelli说道。"所以让我们看看练习赛会如何发展。"
"如果车队要求我这样做，我会做的。因为显然我不是在争夺……当然，能拿到杆位我还是会很高兴，但我是从队尾发车的，所以如果我能做点什么来帮助车队，我会做的。"
对于通常从前列或接近前列发车的这个赛季来说，从队尾发车给了Antonelli一个不寻常的挑战，但他认为"从某种程度上这有助于释放压力"，并且他"心态上非常自由"。
当然，说起来容易，而如何把损失降到最低将是对他心理承受力的一次考验。—— Edd Straw
蒙扎将是对本田最新引擎更真实的考验
费尔南多·阿隆索对自己在F1的未来仍然态度含糊，但他认为蒙扎将就本田最新F1引擎升级所取得的进步提供一个清晰得多的图景。
阿隆索称自己在赞德福特获得第九名对阿斯顿·马丁来说是一次“不错的提振”，这有助于验证B规格底盘所选定的研发方向，并表示“最终我们会成为弯道中最快的车队之一”，但他表示为赞德福特安装的新引擎“说实话并不是一个大的提升”。
“可驾驶性是个问题，而且额外的动力在赞德沃特很难感受到，”阿隆索补充道。
“也许蒙扎对这台发动机会是一次更真实的考验，但仍然有很长的路要走——我们必须在两方面都取得进步，明年底盘和发动机都得提升，这是必须的。”
本田承认，它需要努力改进其最新发动机的可驾驶性，让车手们能够真正充分利用这次升级带来的额外动力。
阿隆索认为，蒙扎回归标准的比赛周末形式、安排三次练习赛，将进一步有助于这一进程，并表示他“百分之百信任”本田最终会破解难题。
“我们只需要以某种方式缩短这个流程，”他补充道。
“不幸的是，我们的起步就踏错了脚步，我们推出的这套规则没有达到我们期望的水平，但我毫不怀疑它们最终会达到目标。”
“正如我说过很多次的，我们不想像他们上次那样等上五年或六年。我们想在两年内做到，最多三年。”—— Ben Anderson
奥迪 打出了传动比上的妙招，而 迈凯伦 却放弃了这一选择
奥迪已经使用了其在2026赛季中唯一一次被允许更改齿轮比的机会，而迈凯伦此前透露自己在今年早些时候放弃了这样做。
车队只有一次“小丑牌”机会，但重新配置齿轮比需要付出成本，这让迈凯伦打消了这个念头——尽管在赛季开始前，它就知道自己相对于引擎供应商梅赛德斯错误地选择了过短的齿轮比。
不过，奥迪已经动用了自己的小丑牌，力图改善其首台F1引擎的一个弱点。
“我们做出的这个改变，是我们在今年很早的时候就发现了的问题，我认为这还是为了整体的可驾驶性，这是我们全年一直在对引擎进行改进的主要方向，”加布里埃尔·博托莱托解释道。
“说实话，我不认为这会大幅改善我们的起步，但我认为它总体上会帮助我们在起步表现上更加稳定一些，也许是这样的。”
此外，在湿地和干地条件下，齿轮的工作方式可能会帮助我们让赛车保持得更稳定一些。
对于奥迪来说，问题并不在于齿轮比过短或过长，而更多在于调整各挡位之间的间隔，以尝试改善可驾性。- Josh Suttill
虽然法拉利正借助F1额外发展与升级机会排名的规则，在蒙扎推出升级版'ADUO 2'规格引擎，但Ollie Bearman所在的哈斯车队是唯一将使用该引擎的客户赛车。
这是因为法拉利只能为其升级版动力单元提供足够的数量，供哈斯车队和凯迪拉克车队各使用一台，使两支车队都处于尴尬的境地。
凯迪拉克选择不使用它，但哈斯车队——他们也在蒙扎首次带来了一个相当大的空气动力学升级——将由贝尔曼来使用它。
"是的，这当然是考量因素之一，"领队小松礼雄在被问到积分榜位置（贝尔曼有18分，而奥孔只有3分）是否起了作用时说道。
"但是，再说一次，最近两次，比如说，不是空气动力学方面的升级，而是我们的一些部件，比如CI [Carbon Industrie]刹车测试，埃斯特班实际上在刹车锁死等方面更挣扎，所以考虑到那次蒙特利尔的升级，我们先把它装在了奥利的车上。"
“我们决定先把刹车升级给Esteban。另外，在动力转向方面，我们在布达佩斯停赛前还有一次动力转向升级。我们决定把那个也给Esteban，因为他对这件事表达得更强烈，而且他在动力转向手感上遇到的困难更多。”
“最近两次升级我们都给了Esteban，所以这次轮到Ollie了。”
Komatsu说“我们没有任何隐藏的议程”，因为在向车手说明时会“没有必要胡扯”。 - JS
比赛初段对凯迪拉克来说将至关重要
在经历了今年多次刹车过热问题之后，凯迪拉克与刹车的斗争仍在继续。
瓦尔特利·博塔斯此前将此形容为气流和零部件问题的混合因素，而在周四他表示，本站可用的“比以前更坚固的刹车导管材料”是一个关键的改进领域。在正常运行情况下，蒙扎不应构成刹车冷却方面的挑战，但他强调意大利大奖赛的前几圈是这方面的关键阶段。
“按照我们的数据，我们应该没问题，但很难模拟的是车流的影响，尤其是当多辆车排成火车般跟车时，”博塔斯说，“那时你在直道上得不到足够的气流。所以我会说比赛的前一部分对我们来说将是最关键的。”
在“纯气流方面仍有进一步的工作要做”，但凯迪拉克在改善这一弱点方面已经取得了重大进展。
detailEn: No circuit is more synonymous with Formula 1 engine performance than Italian Grand Prix host Monza.
So is it any wonder talk of slipstreams (and associated tactics), engine upgrades, and even the raceability of these 2026 F1 cars dominated conversations in the paddock on Thursday?
Here are the biggest takeaways ahead of the on-track action kicking off on Friday:
Kimi Antonelli will start from the back of the Monza grid whatever happens in qualifying thanks to a power unit penalty.

That means he's got nothing tangible to fight for in terms of starting position in qualifying, and on a weekend where slipstreaming is expected to be beneficial he's willing to help out team-mate, and title rival, George Russell if asked. (Something that the non-engine-penalised Charles Leclerc will also do for Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton.)
"It has been discussed with the team, and yes we have agreed on a few things," said Antonelli, when asked by The Race if he's willing to tow Russell. "So let's see how the session develops.

"If the team will ask me to do so, I will do it. Because obviously I'm not fighting for...Of course, I will still be happy to do pole, but I'm starting at the back so if I could do anything to to help the team, I will do."

Starting from the back gives Antonelli an unusual challenge in a season where he's usually started at or near the front, but he argued that "in some ways it helps to release pressure" and that he's "very free mentally".
Of course, that's easy to say, and limiting the damage will be a test of his mental strength. - Edd Straw
Monza will be truer test of Honda's latest engine
Fernando Alonso remains coy on his own F1 future, but he thinks Monza will provide a much clearer picture as regards the step Honda's taken with its latest F1 engine upgrade.

Alonso called his ninth-place finish at Zandvoort a "nice boost" for Aston Martin, helping validate the development direction taken with the B-spec chassis and suggesting "eventually we will be one of the fastest in the corners", but he said the new engine fitted for Zandvoort "was not a big improvement, to be honest".
"The driveability was a problem and the extra power was difficult to feel in Zandvoort," Alonso added.
"Maybe Monza is going to be a more true test for the engine, but still a long way to go - and we need to improve in both ends, in chassis and on engine for next year, it's a must."
Honda accepts it has work to do to improve the driveability of its latest engine and allow the drivers to properly exploit the extra power derived from the update.
Alonso felt the return to the standard weekend format of three practice sessions at Monza will further aid that process and he said he has "100% trust" Honda will eventually crack the code.
"We just need to shortcut somehow that process," he added.
"Unfortunately, we started with the wrong foot and we started with this set of regulations not at the level that we wanted, but I have no doubts that they will get there.
"As I said many times we don't want to wait five years like they did last time, or six years. We want to do it in two years or three years maximum." - Ben Anderson
Audi plays gear-ratio joker that McLaren's declined
Audi has taken its one permitted opportunity to change its gear ratios during the 2026 season, a move McLaren revealed it declined to make earlier this year.

Teams only get one joker, but there's a cost involved in reconfiguring them that put McLaren off doing so - despite knowing it had erroneously picked gear ratios that were too short compared to engine supplier Mercedes before the season began.
Audi has taken its joker, though, as it looks to improve a weakness with its first F1 engine.

"This change we have made, it was something we spotted quite early in the year, and I think it's just, again, for overall driveability, that's the main thing we have been working with our engine through the whole year now," Gabriel Bortoleto explained.
"I don't think it's going to improve our starts massively, if I'm very honest, but I think it's going to help us overall to be a bit more consistent on the performance of the starts, maybe.
"Also in wet conditions, in dry conditions, the way the gears are going to work is probably going to help us a little bit on keeping the car a little bit more stable."
For Audi, it wasn't a case of having too short or too long a gear ratio, but was more about adjusting the steps between them to try and improve driveability. - Josh Suttill

While Ferrari is introducing its upgraded 'ADUO 2' specification engine at Monza, courtesy of the ruling of F1's Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities ranking, Ollie Bearman's Haas is the only customer car that will run it.
That's because Ferrari could only supply enough of its upgraded power units for Haas and Cadillac to have one each, putting both teams in an uncomfortable position.
Cadillac elected not to run it, but Haas, also debuting a sizeable aerodynamic upgrade at Monza, will do so with Bearman.
"Yeah, of course that's part of the consideration," team principal Ayao Komatsu said when asked if championship position (Bearman has 18 points to Ocon's three) played a role.

"But, again, the last two, let's say, not aerodynamic upgrades, but items we had, like CI [Carbon Industrie] brakes test, Esteban was actually struggling more on the brake locking etc so considering that Montreal upgrade, we got it on Ollie first.

"We decided to give the brake upgrade to Esteban first. Also, in terms of power steering, we had another upgrade on the power steering before shutdown in Budapest. We decided to give that to Esteban because, again, he was more vocal about it and he was struggling more [with] the power steering feel.
"The last two upgrades we gave it to Esteban, so this time around, it's back to Ollie."
Komatsu said "we don't have any hidden agenda" because there's "no point bulls***ting" when telling the drivers about it. - JS
Early-race phase will be critical for Cadillac
Cadillac's battle with its brakes continues after myriad overheating problems this year.

Valtteri Bottas has previously characterised this as a mixture of airflow and component problems, and on Thursday referred to "even more robust material than before in the brake ducts" available here as a key area of improvement. Monza should not pose a brake-cooling challenge in normal running, but he highlighted the early laps of the Italian GP as the critical phase for this.

"In our numbers, we should be OK but what is quite hard to simulate is the traffic effect, especially if there's multiple cars in a train," said Botas. "That's when you get the lack of airflow on the straights. So I would say the first part of the race is going to be the most critical for us."
There are still "further steps to make in terms of the pure airflow", but Cadillac has made significant progress in improving this weakness.
